title: Identifying System-on-Chip Security Assets with Structure-Based Analysis
problem: SoC designs integrate components from multiple sources, creating complex attack surfaces; identifying and protecting security assets (cryptographic keys, sensitive data, control logic) is critical but currently manual and time-intensive, slowing security validation and risk assessment.
motivation: SoC complexity and supply-chain risk demand automated security asset identification early in design for faster and more accurate vulnerability assessment.
method: Automated framework for SoC security asset identification: transforms RTL code into graph representations, applies deep neural networks (DNNs) to classify nodes as security or non-security assets based on structural patterns learned from training data. Graph representation captures connectivity and data flow information.
key_novelty: DNN-based classification of RTL-derived structural graphs to automatically identify security assets, eliminating manual identification bottleneck.
contributions: Automated security asset identification framework for SoCs
DNN classifier for security asset classification based on structural patterns
limitations: Evaluation scope (specific SoC designs, tool/library usage patterns) not detailed; generalization to diverse RTL coding styles; false positive/negative impact on subsequent security verification; transferability across different design teams not discussed.
primary_theme: DNN-based automated security asset identification from RTL structural analysis
